CITY COUNCIL MEETING FOR JUNE 7, 2021 AT

In order to facilitate public participation at meetings held solely by
electronic means, the City will accept public comment in the following
manner:
1. During the meeting, members of the public may provide live public
comment by submitting a speaker card prior to the start of public
comment on that item, at the following webpage:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/public-comment
If a public comment speaker wishes to speak on more than one agenda
item, please indicate so on the online form (multiple item speakers will
be handled according to the process posted on the agenda and as
specified in the City Council meeting policy). Public comments are
limited to 3 minutes each, and the Mayor and City Council may limit this
time if reasonable under the circumstances.
2. Speaker
Card Help Line : If a public comment speaker needs assistance in
completing a speaker card,
please call the City Clerk�s Office at: (626) 744-4124.
Help line will open
30 minutes prior to the posted start time of the meeting.
After submitting a public speaker card, join the virtual meeting after
the published start time with a computer, other electronic device, or by
telephone. The same name or telephone number on the Speaker Card should
be used for the virtual meeting in order to locate and unmute the
speaker.
Computer or electronic devices, join the meeting at:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/161482446
Telephone only dial-in: 1-669-900-6833, Meeting ID: 161 482 446
3.
Members of the public may submit correspondence of any length prior to
the start of the meeting, at the following email address:
correspondence@cityofpasadena.net
Correspondence will be forwarded to the City Council prior to the
start of the meeting, posted online, and made part of the legislative
record for the item.

  of allegiance was led by Council member Williams.

CEREMONIAL MATTERS  Mayor Gordo reported on the Pride Month Flag Raising ceremony
  held earlier at City Hall, expressed appreciation and thanks to all
  staff and community members involved, and provided special
  appreciation to Councilmember Kennedy for recommending the
  City's acknowledgment of Pride Month.

  Mayor Gordo presented a commendation to the Women's City Club
  of Pasadena recognizing their 75 years of extraordinary benefit and
  service to its members and the community in the City of Pasadena.
  Suzanne Burger, President of the Women's City Club of Pasadena,
  accepted the commendation, spoke on the transfer of ownership of
  the Blinn House to Pasadena Heritage, and thanked the members
  of the Women's City Club of Pasadena, the City Council and
  community. Sue Mossman, Executive Director of Pasadena
  Heritage, and Brian Alan Baker, President of Blinn House
  Foundation and Board Chair of Pasadena Heritage, expressed
  appreciation to the Women's City Club of Pasadena for their 75
  years of service to the community, and thanked Mayor Gordo, the
  City Council, and community for their support.

  Councilmember Kennedy spoke on the services provided by the
  Women's City Club of Pasadena and thanked the members for their
  work in the community.

  Councilmembers Kennedy and Hampton spoke on the passing of
  Dr. Dorothy A. Evans, Pastor at Refuge Christian Center located in
  Pasadena, noted her work as a community activist, and requested
  that the meeting be adjourned in her memory.

   Vice Mayor Wilson and Councilmember Madison, summarized the
  Ad Hoc Committee's discussion related to the Independent Police
  Auditor selection process and responded to questions.

  Michele Beal Bagneris, City Attorney/City Prosecutor, provided
  information related to staff ensuring that all applicants meet the
  requirement of the City's ordinance related to the creation of a
  Community Police Oversight Commission (CPOC) and an
  Independent Police Auditor (IPA); and responded to questions.

  MOTION:  It was moved by Councilmember Kennedy, Seconded by
  Councilmember Madison , to approve the appointments of the
  CPOC and the staff recommendation related to the Authorization to
  Enter Into a Contract with the Maxey Group, LLD dba Modern
  Policing for Independent Police Auditor Services:
  (MOTION WITHDRAWN)

  Councilmember Rivas expressed concerns with information on
  Modern Policing's (recommended Independent Police Auditor
  contractor) website which displays information that Mr. Brian Maxey
  is a Washington State Certified Police Officer; and questioned how
  his resume, which includes working as a defense attorney for police
  officers in civil rights cases for over a decade, will be perceived by
  the community.

  Brian Maxey, representing Modern Policing, explained that while
  working at the Seattle Police Department as a civilian overseeing
  the implementation of best practices for the federal Consent
  Decree, he was encouraged to increase his education by attending
  the police academy, resulting in his certification as a Washington
  Peace Officer. He noted, however, that he has never been a
  commissioned police officer; and responded to questions. He stated
  the he is willing to step down if the CPOC determines he is not the
  right individual for the position of IPA.

  Councilmember Kennedy stated the following , "Let the record
  reflect, that staff... City Staff told me that that particular applicant
  was not qualified and that is why she did not receive an interview. I
  was going on the ... I suppose review of staff, and I believe without
  going into detail, the information that was provided to me, by staff
  was accurate, but there was no way to deny Ms. Abdullah an
  opportunity to serve. But you had to meet the qualifications and staff
  told me that there was an issue with the application." and "For the
  record I will tell you that I'm okay with OIR Group . The City Manager
  has retained their services for the review, if I understand it correctly,
  in the officer involved shooting concerning Anthony McClain, but I
  am troubled by the fact that certain members of the Committee said
  they did not know of Brian Maxey's background."

Council Minutes  15  06/07/2021
   Councilmembers Madison, Williams, and Hampton voiced support
  for the staff recommendation. Councilmember Williams stated that
  as part of the Ad Hoc Committee she was fully aware of Brian
  Maxey's background.

  At the request of Councilmember Hampton, City Attorney Bagneris
  stated that staff will include a provision in the contract that allows
  the City to terminate the contract for convenience for any reason or
  for no reason. The City Council as the approving authority would be
  the entity to terminate the contract, and staff can include language
  in the contract that if the CPOC determines not to continue the
  contract with Modern Policing, the matter should be referred to the
  City Council for consideration.

  City Clerk Jomsky provided the following information related to the
  staggered terms of the CPOC members, which coincides with the
